newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X falls as deadline approaches.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X falls as deadline approaches.

text.p: Trading was brisk in Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp shares on Monday as the market speculated about ongoing negotiations between the two gold companies.

The Indonesian government has asked Bre-X to carve up its huge Busang gold deposit in Indonesia by handing over 75 percent of its stake in the project to Barrick. The companies have until Wednesday to come to an agreement, or the Indonesian government will step in, Bre-X has said.
As the Wednesday deadline approaches, trading in Bre-X and Barrick is becoming more volatile, analysts said.
By midday Monday, Bre-X had dropped C$1.55 to 19.10 in trading of 3.5 million shares, topping the most-actives list for the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Barrick had fallen C$0.65 to 39.85, with 1.7 million shares trading hands, though at least part of the slide may be because of the weaker gold price, analysts said.
As the Wednesday deadline approaches, rumors putting Bre-X in a poor light are swirling, analysts said.
They noted Bre-X has little room to manoeuvre in its talks with Barrick, since the Indonesian government has given the company no choice in partners.
Many investors had expected Bre-X and Barrick to have reached an agreement by now and are starting to get discouraged, analysts said.
"It's a very fluid and flaky market," said one analyst.
Bre-X would not comment on the state of negotiations and Barrick could not be reached for comment.
Trading in Bre-X has been volatile and plagued by rumors since earlier this fall when it announced it would start searching for a major mining company to act as operator of the deposit.

Earlier on Monday, Indonesian businessman Jusuf Merukh told Reuters in Jakarta that he had put off a US$1.9 million lawsuit against Bre-X because the Calgary-based company had begun discussions with him over the Busang find.
Merukh has claimed up to 40 percent of the discovery.
